verses.zh: 我说：雅各的首领，以色列家的官长啊，你们要听！你们不当知道公平吗？
verses.en: I said,“Listen, you leaders[NOTE:1] of Jacob,you rulers of the nation[NOTE:2] of Israel!You ought to know what is just,[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “heads.”
Heb “house.”
Heb “Should you not know justice?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course you should!”

verses.zh: 你们恶善好恶，从人身上剥皮，从人骨头上剔肉，
verses.en: yet you[NOTE:1] hate what is good[NOTE:2] and love what is evil.[NOTE:3] You flay my people’s skin[NOTE:4] and rip the flesh from their bones.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the ones who.”
Or “good.”
Or “evil.”

Heb “their skin from upon them.” The referent of the pronoun (“my people,” referring to Jacob and/or the house of Israel, with the Lord as the speaker) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “and their flesh from their bones.”sn Micah compares the social injustice perpetrated by the house of Jacob/Israel to cannibalism because it threatens the very lives of the oppressed.

verses.zh: 吃我民的肉，剥他们的皮，打折他们的骨头，分成块子像要下锅，又像釜中的肉。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] devour my people’s flesh,strip off their skin,and crush their bones.You chop them up like flesh in a pot[NOTE:2]—like meat in a kettle.
notes: Heb “who.”
The MT reads “and they chop up as in a pot.” The translation assumes an emendation of כַּאֲשֶׁר (ka’asher, “as”) to כִּשְׁאֵר (kishʾer, “like flesh”).

verses.zh: 到了遭灾的时候，这些人必哀求耶和华，他却不应允他们。那时他必照他们所行的恶事向他们掩面。
verses.en: Someday these sinful leaders[NOTE:1] will cry to the Lord for help,but he will not answer them.He will hide his face from them at that time,because they have done such wicked deeds.”
notes: Heb “they,” referring to the indicted leaders in vv. 1-3.

verses.zh: 论到使我民走差路的先知―他们牙齿有所嚼的，他们就呼喊说：平安了！凡不供给他们吃的，他们就预备攻击他（预备攻击他：或译说必遭遇刀兵）―耶和华如此说：
verses.en: This is what the Lord has said about the prophets who mislead my people,[NOTE:1] “If someone gives them enough to eat,they offer an oracle of peace.[NOTE:2] But if someone does not give them food,they are ready to declare war on him.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “concerning the prophets, those who mislead my people.” Some prefer to begin the quotation after “the Lord has said” (cf. NIV). But when the preposition עַל (ʿal, “about”) occurs with this introductory formula it regularly indicates who is being spoken about. (When a person is not the object of the preposition, it may begin the quote, meaning “because.”) Including the first person pronominal suffix (in “my people”) after a third person introduction may sound awkward, but also occurs in Jer 14:15; 23:2 (and perhaps Jer 12:14, a text critical question). Hillers prefers to add הוֹי (hoy, “woe, ah”) at the beginning of the quotation, after the graphically similar יְהוָה (yehvah; see D. R. Hillers, Micah [Hermeneia], 44). The phrase הוֹי עַל (hoy ʿal, “woe upon”) occurs in Jer 50:27 and Ezek 13:3 (with “the prophets” following the preposition in the latter instance).

Heb “those who bite with their teeth and cry out, ‘peace.’” The phrase “bite with the teeth” is taken here as idiomatic for eating. Apparently these prophets were driven by mercenary motives. If they were paid well, they gave positive oracles to their clients, but if someone could not afford to pay them, they were hostile and delivered oracles of doom.
Heb “but [as for the one] who does not place [food] in their mouths, they prepare for war against him.”

verses.zh: 你们必遭遇黑夜，以致不见异象；又必遭遇幽暗，以致不能占卜。日头必向你们沉落，白昼变为黑暗。
verses.en: Therefore night will fall, and you will receive no visions;[NOTE:1] it will grow dark, and you will no longer be able to read the omens.[NOTE:2] The sun will set on these prophets,and the daylight will turn to darkness over their heads.[NOTE:3]
notes: The coming of night (and darkness in the following line) symbolizes the cessation of revelation.tn Heb “it will be night for you without a vision.”

The reading of omens (Heb “divination”) was forbidden in the law (Deut 18:10), so this probably reflects the prophets’ view of how they received divine revelation.tn Heb “it will be dark for you without divination.”
Heb “and the day will be dark over them.”

verses.zh: 先见必抱愧，占卜的必蒙羞，都必捂着嘴唇，因为　神不应允他们。
verses.en: The prophets[NOTE:1] will be ashamed;the omen readers will be humiliated.All of them will cover their mouths,[NOTE:2] for they will receive no divine oracles.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “seers.”
Or “the mustache,” or perhaps “the beard.” Cf. KJV, NAB, NRSV “cover their lips.”
Heb “no divine response” or “no answer from God.”

verses.zh: 至于我，我藉耶和华的灵，满有力量、公平、才能，可以向雅各说明他的过犯，向以色列指出他的罪恶。
verses.en: But I[NOTE:1] am full of the courage that the Lord’s Spirit givesand have a strong commitment to justice.[NOTE:2] This enables me to confront Jacob with its rebellionand Israel with its sin.[NOTE:3]
notes: The prophet Micah speaks here and contrasts himself with the mercenaries just denounced by the Lord in the preceding verses.

Heb “am full of power, the Spirit of the Lord, and justice and strength.” The appositional phrase “the Spirit of the Lord” explains the source of the prophet’s power. The phrase “justice and strength” is understood here as a hendiadys, referring to the prophet’s strong sense of justice.
Heb “to declare to Jacob his rebellion and to Israel his sin.” The words “this enables me” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 雅各家的首领、以色列家的官长啊，当听我的话！你们厌恶公平，在一切事上屈枉正直；
verses.en: Listen to this, you leaders of the family[NOTE:1] of Jacob,you rulers of the nation[NOTE:2] of Israel!You[NOTE:3] hate justiceand pervert all that is right.
notes: Heb “house.”
Heb “house.”
Heb “who.” A new sentence was begun here in the translation for stylistic reasons (also at the beginning of v. 10).

verses.zh: 以人血建立锡安，以罪孽建造耶路撒冷。
verses.en: You[NOTE:1] build Zion through bloody crimes,[NOTE:2] Jerusalem[NOTE:3] through unjust violence.
notes: Heb “who.”
Heb “bloodshed” (so NAB, NASB, NIV); NLT “murder.”
For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

verses.zh: 首领为贿赂行审判；祭司为雇价施训诲；先知为银钱行占卜。他们却倚赖耶和华，说：耶和华不是在我们中间吗？灾祸必不临到我们。
verses.en: Her[NOTE:1] leaders take bribes when they decide legal cases,[NOTE:2] her priests proclaim rulings for profit,and her prophets read omens for pay.Yet they claim to trust[NOTE:3] the Lord and say,“The Lord is among us.[NOTE:4] Disaster will not overtake[NOTE:5] us!”
notes: The pronoun Her refers to Jerusalem (note the previous line).
Heb “judge for a bribe.”
Heb “they lean upon” (so KJV, NIV84, NRSV); NAB “rely on”; NIV11 “look for support.”
Heb “Is not the Lord in our midst?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course he is!”
Or “come upon” (so many English versions); NCV “happen to us”; CEV “come to us.”

verses.zh: 所以因你们的缘故，锡安必被耕种像一块田，耶路撒冷必变为乱堆；这殿的山必像丛林的高处。
verses.en: Therefore, because of you,[NOTE:1] Zion will be plowed up like[NOTE:2] a field,Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins,and the Temple Mount[NOTE:3] will become a hill overgrown with brush![NOTE:4]
notes: The plural pronoun refers to the leaders, priests, and prophets mentioned in the preceding verse.
Or “into” (an adverbial accusative of result).
Heb “the mountain of the house” (so KJV, ASV, NRSV).
Heb “a high place of overgrowth.”
